text:
[title] Block tables
[body] KV-cache split into fixed-size blocks, mapped per sequence
[body] Copy-on-write shares blocks across parallel samples
[body] Prefix caching hit rate: 61% on the chat workload

novice.takeaway: The slide describes a memory management technique called 'block tables' that splits and shares AI model memory efficiently, improving reuse of cached data.
questions: What is KV-cache in this context?
How does prefix caching improve performance?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants us to believe block tables are a key technique enabling the earlier claimed speed improvements.

peer.takeaway: The system organizes the KV-cache into fixed-size blocks with per-sequence mapping, copy-on-write sharing, and prefix caching to improve memory efficiency.
questions: How do block tables map blocks to sequences?
What causes prefix cache hits/misses here?
How does this relate to PagedAttention from slide 3?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe block tables are a key mechanism enabling the earlier claimed memory efficiency gains.

expert.takeaway: The slide describes PagedAttention's block-table mechanism (fixed-size KV-cache blocks, copy-on-write sharing) and reports a 61% prefix cache hit rate on a chat workload.
questions: Which chat workload/benchmark was used for the 61% figure?
How does block size affect the hit rate?
Does hit rate vary across other workload types?
expert.inferred_claim: Block-table based memory management with copy-on-write and prefix caching contributes to the system's serving efficiency gains.

slide_intent.text: Block-table based memory management with copy-on-write sharing and prefix caching achieves high cache efficiency and improves serving performance.
